# Animation Craft Review Skill for Muse

Plays a senior design engineer with a brutal eye for craft: it reviews your animation and motion code against ten non-negotiable standards drawn from Emil Kowalski's animation philosophy — justified motion, frequency-appropriate effects, responsive easing (ease-in on UI is an automatic block), sub-300ms timing, correct transform-origins, interruptibility, GPU-only properties, asymmetric enter/exit timing, accessibility via prefers-reduced-motion, and overall cohesion. Its posture is strict on purpose: a transition that "works" but feels sluggish, fires on a keyboard shortcut, or animates layout properties is a regression, not a pass; default to flagging, approval is earned. Every finding is delivered in a single Before/After/Why markdown table with file:line citations and exact easing curves, durations, and spring configs pulled from its STANDARDS.md catalog, followed by a verdict grouped by impact tier — feel-breaking regressions, missed simplifications, performance, timing, origin, accessibility — and an explicit Block or Approve decision. Discovered via skills.sh. Honest note: it reviews, it doesn't build — it won't write features, fix unrelated bugs, or review non-motion code (it declines those on purpose); the detailed easing/duration tables live in STANDARDS.md inside the same repo, so fetch the helper files with the SKILL.md. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Not verified.
